title: Grandma's recipe box
summary: A family tries to cook a dish from a recipe that is missing one important line.
paragraphs: After Grandma Rosa moved into a smaller flat, she gave her wooden recipe box to her granddaughter, Julia. It was full of cards written in her careful handwriting, with brown spots of oil on the corners. Julia's favourite was "Sunday rice", the dish that the family had eaten every week for thirty years.

The next Sunday, Julia decided to cook it for everyone. She followed the card exactly: rice, chicken, red peppers, garlic, a little {{saffron}}, water and salt. The kitchen smelled wonderful. But when the family sat down and tasted it, there was a {{polite}} silence. It was good, but it wasn't Grandma's.

Julia tried again the next week, and the week after that. She changed the rice, the pan and the amount of water. Her brother suggested more salt. Her father thought the chicken should be fried for longer. Nothing worked. The rice was always nice, but something was missing.

Finally she took the card to Grandma Rosa. Grandma read it, laughed and took a pencil from her bag. At the bottom of the card she wrote one more line: "A spoonful of the {{broth}} from Saturday's soup." "I never wrote that," she said, "because there was always soup on Saturday."

Now Julia makes soup every Saturday, even in summer, and on Sundays the family eats rice that tastes exactly like it used to. She has started her own box of cards. On each one, at the bottom, she writes the {{secret}} steps that are too ordinary to remember: "Use the old pan", "Wait until it smells sweet", "Make extra for Grandma".

saffron.meaning: a red-orange spice that gives food a yellow colour

polite.meaning: kind and correct in the way you behave

broth.meaning: a thin soup made by boiling meat or vegetables in water

secret.meaning: something that only a few people know

questions.question: What was the problem with Julia's first "Sunday rice"?
options: It was good but did not taste like Grandma's.
questions.explanation: It was good, but it wasn't Grandma's.

questions.question: What did Julia's family suggest?
options: More salt and frying the chicken for longer
Buying the rice at a restaurant
questions.explanation: Her brother suggested more salt, and her father thought the chicken should be fried longer.

questions.question: Why was the last line missing from the card?
options: Grandma wanted to keep it secret.
There was always soup on Saturday, so Grandma never thought of writing it.
Julia lost part of the card.
questions.explanation: Grandma said she never wrote it because there was always soup on Saturday.

questions.question: What does Julia write on her own recipe cards?
options: Ordinary steps that people forget to write down
The names of the people who like the dish
questions.explanation: She writes the secret steps that are too ordinary to remember.
